zonesList.title: Zones
zonesList.structureHint: A zone is a group of similar assets inside a point, with its own accounting mode and rates: “Cars”, “Trampoline”, “Playroom”. An asset is a single unit inside a zone: one car, one trampoline. Employees submit results per asset.
zonesList.noZones: No zones yet — add the first one below.
zonesList.newZoneSub: A group of attractions within a point
zonesList.accountingModeLaunchesHint: A ready ride count per submission
zonesList.accountingModeCashOnlyHint: No tariffs or assets — just the amount
zonesList.accountingModeTicketsHint: Ticket sales by order, redemption optional
zonesList.accountingModeTooltip: Pick by how your staff will record the zone’s work — details are in the ⓘ next to each mode. You can change the mode until the zone has its first results submission; after that it is locked for good.
zonesList.accountingModeCountersTooltip: There are two ways to get the reading — switched by the “Readings from sessions” toggle on the zone card. Off: the machine counts sessions itself on a mechanical counter, staff record nothing during the day and copy the number off the counter once at the submission. On: there may be no counter at all — staff tap the asset for each session, the system adds the reading up itself, and nothing is entered at the submission. Either way revenue = the difference from the previous submission × the tariff price, and there are no more than two tariffs.
zonesList.accountingModeLaunchesTooltip: Staff log each ride with a tap on the asset — a digital replacement for the notebook with tally marks. The system knows the ride count itself; nothing is entered by hand. A tariff can be plain (the tap counts the ride right away) or timed (the tap starts a countdown and the asset stays busy until stopped). Up to four tariffs per zone.
zonesList.accountingModeStaysTooltip: Real-time tracking: staff open a visit at the entrance and close it at the exit, one per visitor. Fits places where the length of the visit matters: the price can be flat per entry or per minute. The owner does not watch individual visits — only the shift total.
zonesList.accountingModeTicketsTooltip: Selling tickets as orders. Sale and use are separated in time: a ticket sold today can be redeemed tomorrow, and by a different staff member. Redemption can be turned off entirely, and then the system only knows about sales. Prices are not set by tariffs but on the assets themselves: each has its own ticket options.
zonesList.accountingModeCashOnlyTooltip: No assets, no tariffs. Staff enter a single amount per shift — cash and card. There is no calculated revenue, so there is nothing to compare the Difference against: the system simply records what was handed in.

zoneDetail.amountRoundingHint: The "actual time" launch amount is rounded to the nearest whole currency unit: below half — down, half and above — up
zoneDetail.ticketRedemptionHint: Off — the system only knows sales, no statuses or redemption ("old-school")
zoneDetail.ticketVariantsEmptyError: Add at least one named variant
zoneDetail.gameRoomRateHint: Example: 1 ₽ — 45 minutes of stay will cost 45 ₽.
zoneDetail.gameRoomRoundingUpNote: Duration is rounded up to the full minute — the point never loses money on partial minutes.
zoneDetail.gameRoomUseSingleRateButton: Switch back to a single price
zoneDetail.launchesTimedTariffHint: Launch runs a countdown; asset is busy until stopped/released
zoneDetail.assetsTooltip: An asset is a single physical unit inside the zone: one particular car, trampoline or console. Results are submitted per asset, so each keeps its own history and its own readings. Deactivate a broken asset instead of deleting it — deleting also removes its past submissions.
zoneDetail.tariffsTooltipCounters: A tariff is the price of one session. Each tariff has its own count on the asset, so the zone’s revenue is the sum across tariffs: sessions × price. Tests and refunds that staff enter at the submission are subtracted from it. No more than two tariffs: that is how many separate counters fit on the device, and with readings from sessions the taps are split the same way.
zoneDetail.tariffsTooltipLaunches: A tariff is the price of one session. “No timer” — staff simply tap to log the session. “With timer” — the session runs on a countdown and the asset counts as busy until it is stopped or released.
zoneDetail.tariffsTooltipStays: A tariff is the price of a stay. “Per entry” — a flat amount no matter how long the visit lasts. “Per actual time” — a per-minute price: the system counts the time from start to stop and rounds up to a whole minute.

readings.title: Daily results
readings.cashLeftTooltip: Cash for the day minus expenses and minus the bonuses and advances the employee took from the till. Card payments and payments from a balance are not included — that money is not in the till. Collections are not counted either: this is the day's result, not the current balance at the location.

readings.differenceTooltip: Difference = actual cash − calculated revenue. What was paid from a balance is not part of the calculated revenue: that money came in earlier, when the balance was topped up, and could not reach this submission's till. Zero means everything adds up.
readings.goodsDifferenceTooltip: What the employee handed over minus what the system counted from goods sales. Zero means it matches; minus is a shortfall, plus means more was handed in. Payments from a balance are excluded: that money came in earlier, at top-up.
readings.actualCashTooltip: Cash and card handed over by the employee. Expenses are already accounted for: the employee enters what is left in the till after spending. Payments from a balance are not included — that money came in earlier, when the balance was topped up.

workTime.bonusAccruedTooltip: An accrued bonus is added to the staff member’s “to pay out” balance but was never handed over in cash — the point’s till never saw it. A regular bonus, by contrast, has already left the till as cash.

onboarding.welcomeBody: Install demo data to see how everything works right away? A point, two zones with assets and tariffs, an employee — you can freely rename or delete them later.

operatorGuide.intro: A short guide to working in the app. Only what applies to you.
operatorGuide.timeAuto: is tracked automatically — tap “Start shift” when you arrive and “End shift” when you leave
operatorGuide.timeManual: you enter yourself: at the end of the day add a shift — when you arrived and when you left
operatorGuide.timeNote: Until a shift is started, time for that day is not counted.
operatorGuide.countersText: Copy the number from the counter display exactly as it is — the app works out the launches itself. Even if the counter reached its limit and started from zero again.
operatorGuide.countersTapText: Mark every launch by tapping the asset tile — there is nothing to copy down.
operatorGuide.returnsText: The launch did not happen, the child changed their mind, you were testing it yourself — mark a refund. Otherwise the app will expect money for it and the till will not add up.
operatorGuide.staysText: A guest arrives — open a stay and it gets a number. They leave — stop it. Cancel a stay opened by mistake: while it is open, time keeps running and the amount keeps growing.
operatorGuide.staysRoundingText: Where payment is by time, the final amount is rounded to whole units.
operatorGuide.launchesText: One tap on an asset — one launch.
operatorGuide.launchesTimerText: On timed rates a tap starts the countdown: when the time is up the app gives a signal — stop the launch.
operatorGuide.ticketsText: A sale is an order: fill the cart, take the payment, and you get an order number.
operatorGuide.ticketsRedemptionText: At the entrance you find the order by its number and redeem the tickets. The sale and the entry can happen on different days and with different staff — that is normal.
operatorGuide.ticketsLockText: If you work at one spot — pick it in the asset list and close the lock: other people’s sales will not clutter your list and your choice will not reset. You can unlock it in the same place, with a confirmation.
operatorGuide.paymentsText: Choose how they pay: cash or cashless.
operatorGuide.paymentsBalanceText: You can also charge the customer’s balance — if there is enough on it.
operatorGuide.paymentsSplitText: They pay in parts — tap “Split payment” and enter the amounts.
operatorGuide.balanceNote: Payment from a balance is not money in the till: it came in earlier, when the balance was topped up.
operatorGuide.abonementsText: Open “Customers”, find the person by phone number or add a new one. To sell a subscription — pick it and take the payment: the amount goes onto the customer’s balance, usually more than they paid — the owner gives the difference as a bonus.
operatorGuide.balanceSpendCountersText: A customer is riding off their balance — open “Counters”, find them and charge the amount. That is the only place to charge a balance; “Customers” is for top-ups only.
operatorGuide.goodsText: A sale takes the item off the stock straight away.
operatorGuide.goodsHeldText: The guest has picked things up but pays later — create a held order and give it a name (“Table by the window”). It waits in the list until they settle up.
operatorGuide.goodsBalanceText: Goods can also be paid for from the customer’s balance.
operatorGuide.goodsRevisionText: The stock does not match the shelf — run a stock check: count the goods and enter the actual quantity.
operatorGuide.goodsNoRevisionText: The stock does not match the shelf — tell the owner, do not fix it yourself.
operatorGuide.goodsCashText: The goods till is handed in separately from the zone results — it is its own reconciliation.
operatorGuide.expensesText: You took money out of the till — record the expense right away: the amount, the till and the category.
operatorGuide.expensesCommentText: Always write a comment on what it went on — in a week neither you nor the owner will remember.
operatorGuide.expensesDeleteText: Until the results are submitted, you can delete a wrong expense yourself.
operatorGuide.submitCashText: Cash is what is actually left in the till: count the money and enter what you have on hand.
operatorGuide.submitExpensesText: You do not need to subtract the expenses — the app adds them itself.
operatorGuide.submitByAssetText: The till is entered for each asset separately.
operatorGuide.submitDifferenceText: If it does not add up, you will see the difference. Do not massage the numbers — submit as is, the owner will sort it out.
operatorGuide.printText: The receipt can be printed right after the sale.
operatorGuide.collectionText: You hand money to the owner — record a collection: choose the till and enter the amount handed over. The till balance goes down.
operatorGuide.payoutCashText: You take money for yourself from the point’s till — record it in the app. The amount leaves the balance straight away and the owner sees it.
operatorGuide.payoutAccrualText: A bonus is credited to your balance — no money is taken from the till.
operatorGuide.tasksText: Mark the ones you have done — the owner sees the status.
operatorGuide.mistakeText: Only the owner can edit submitted results — tell them what to fix. Do not submit the results a second time.
operatorGuide.offlineText: The submitted results are saved in the app and will go through on their own once there is a connection. Do not close the app until then.
